purpose: Limit selection for decision 0029, layer A: every successful episode of every canonical paid run, split by arm, with the predeclared formulas applied. No intuition; every chosen value is a stated function of an observed maximum.

measurement_semantics.source: verifiers/<variant>/run/traces.jsonl per run, parsed with the pinned Verifiers build (0.3.1.dev21, commit 7e1c47d24d055aae587ee8259f77a3e8e193513a) from the engine venv, so every quantity is the same computed property the framework limit checks.
measurement_semantics.model_turns: Trace.num_turns = count of trace nodes with sampled=True; this is what RolloutLimits.max_turns caps.
measurement_semantics.intercepted_model_calls: len(Trace.calls) = every intercepted exchange, including provider failures that returned no generation.
measurement_semantics.input_tokens: Trace.num_input_tokens (branch-aware min_new_input_tokens); this is what max_input_tokens caps. Every sampled node in these traces is its own graph leaf, so num_branches == num_turns for all 731 episodes and the quantity equals the sum of per-call input tokens (prompt + cached) — the billable input, not a de-duplicated prefix.
measurement_semantics.output_tokens: Trace.num_output_tokens = sum of completion tokens; what max_output_tokens caps.
measurement_semantics.total_tokens: Trace.num_total_tokens = per-branch final sequence length summed across branches.
measurement_semantics.elapsed_agent_seconds: timing.agent.end - timing.agent.start. This is the stage AgentConfig.timeout.rollout bounds, i.e. the Campaign's execution.timeout_seconds once wired.
measurement_semantics.elapsed_episode_seconds: max(stage end) - timing.start, i.e. boot + setup + agent + finalize + scoring.
measurement_semantics.variant_seconds: execution/real-execution-result.json child_outcome finished_at - started_at: the whole managed eval child, which is what the 1800 s supervisor deadline bounds.
measurement_semantics.soft_overshoot: Token limits are checked between turns, so the turn crossing a cap still completes. A cap of X therefore permits X + one turn.

evidence_scope.note_on_partial_runs: wp11e-0819/journey-partial-a (interrupted, phase running_variants) and wp11e-0819/journey-killed (baseline SIGKILLed, exit -9) contributed 11 successful episodes. They are reported separately; including them changes no maximum in any dimension.

turn_conformance.question: Does the count of intercepted subject-model generations equal Trace.num_turns per episode?

successful_generations_equal_num_turns.definition: len([c for c in trace.calls if c.error is None]) == trace.num_turns; identical result for len([c for c in trace.calls if c.usage is not None])

raw_intercepted_exchanges_equal_num_turn.direction: calls always EXCEED turns, never fall short (deltas: +1 in 18 episodes, +2 in 7, +3 in 2)
raw_intercepted_exchanges_equal_num_turn.cause: 38 intercepted exchanges across 27 episodes failed with ProviderError status 429 (upstream rate limit). Each carries usage=None and node=None: no generation, no node, no tokens, no cost.

turn_conformance.normalized_record_cross_check: normalized-episodes.jsonl num_turns/model_calls agree with the recomputed values on all 720 episodes that carry a normalized record (the 11 partial-run episodes have none).
turn_conformance.verdict: CONFORMS on the billable reading. Every subject generation that actually produced a reply is one num_turns, in 731/731 episodes with zero exceptions. maximum_model_calls -> max_turns is therefore a true mapping for cost and for turn accounting. It is NOT true for the literal count of HTTP exchanges the interception layer saw: a provider 429 is an extra intercepted call that num_turns does not count. Since a 429 costs nothing and produces no turn, this recommends the mapping proceed; the chief should record which reading 'model calls' means in the Campaign's own documentation.

maximum_turns.note: On the raw-intercepted-call reading the observed maximum is 38 and the formula would give 48. The cap is on num_turns, so 44 is the value; 48 is recorded only so the difference is visible.

maximum_input_tokens.formula: 1.5 x max observed, rounded up to a clean number

maximum_output_tokens.formula: keep 8000 if every observed episode sat comfortably below
maximum_output_tokens.margin: NEGATIVE. One successful canonical episode (post1/baseline, task sha256:e08bb7c7a18a..., 25 turns) reached the enforced 8000 cap: stop_condition == 'max_output_tokens', 8212 output tokens after the one-turn soft overshoot. The next highest episode is 7218 output tokens (90.2% of 8000).
maximum_output_tokens.escalation: 0029 says keep 8000 only if every observed episode sat comfortably below; it did not. 0029 also says never auto-raise a cap a canonical run reached - any cap change is another Campaign version. This value is therefore NOT chosen here. The analogous 1.5x rule would give 12318, clean 16000.

maximum_total_tokens.formula: derived in the compiler as maximum_input_tokens + maximum_output_tokens (0029 chief resolution 1); not a declared field
maximum_total_tokens.note: Undetermined until maximum_output_tokens is settled. With input 900000 and output 8000 it would be 908000; with output 16000, 916000.

rollout_timeout_seconds.note: AgentConfig.timeout.rollout bounds the agent solve stage only. Even measured over the whole episode (boot+setup+agent+finalize+scoring) the maximum is 382.0 s, still 218.0 s inside 600.

variant_deadline_seconds.formula: 1800 (named release constant in the child-launch path, 0029 chief resolution 2)
variant_deadline_seconds.observed_maximum_variant: wp11e-recert/first baseline (36 episodes; 19 of them absorbed a provider 429 retry)
variant_deadline_seconds.note: Tightest of the three time bounds: the worst observed variant used 70.1% of the deadline. Every other variant finished under 1041 s. The 429 storm on 2026-08-20 is what stretched it.

cost_bound.formula: tasks x 2 x ((I + C) x input_price + (O + S) x output_price) / 1e6, per decision 0029 layer C and src/techtree/verifiers/budget.py

inputs.context_window_source: release/price-profile.json and src/techtree/verifiers/budget.py; the provider publishes no context ceiling for qwen/qwen3.7-flash in anything this repository carries, so 131072 is the deliberately conservative assumption already recorded there. Nothing in certification-evidence records a context window for this model.
inputs.sampling_cap_source: Campaign agents.subject.sampling.max_tokens = 4096, confirmed identical in all 731 observed traces

candidates.note: zero headroom over the observed maximum; shown only to prove the ceiling is unreachable

largest_input_cap_that_fits_under_1_00.verdict: unusable - it clips 3.3% of successful canonical episodes, which 0029's stop conditions forbid

cost_bound.escalation: BLOCKING for layer A as specified. With the predeclared 1.5x input rule the conservative bound is $2.25 (exact) or $2.35 (clean 900000), against a declared maximum_usd of 1.00, so require_cost_bound would refuse the Campaign before it ran. The gap is structural, not a rounding accident: the input allowance alone is charged 72 times, so any input cap above ~279k tokens breaks $1.00 at $0.03/Mtok, and 24 successful canonical episodes already exceed 279k. Actual observed spend per comparison is $0.16-$0.20, so the Campaign is not really a dollar away from its limit; the bound is deliberately pessimistic. Resolution requires an author/founder decision: raise maximum_usd (a new Campaign version - $2.50 clears 900000/8000 and $2.50 also clears 900000/16000), or change the bound's formula. This worker did not choose.

stop_condition_observations.detail: post1/baseline episode 46c3f1b9c1164d769f8073408d3bb37c, task sha256:e08bb7c7a18a57a83d2ad8dba412c416a8746f708f54b8a29efc0355cabbdb45, stop_condition max_output_tokens at 8212 output tokens against the enforced 8000. The episode still scored (ok=true).
stop_condition_observations.all_other_episodes: stop_condition 'agent_completed' (730/731); no episode was truncated by a length finish_reason.
stop_condition_observations.note: Confirms 0029's premise: of the four declared execution limits only the output ceiling was ever compiled, and execution.timeout_seconds=600 was decorative in all 24 variant configs.
